s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive periorbital swelling with erythema and destructive lesion in the maxillary sinus
salient_findings: Progressive right periorbital swelling of three weeks’ duration
Destructive lesion centered on the anterior wall of the right maxillary sinus
Large soft-tissue mass protruding into the sinus
key_facts: 27-month-old girl
Progressive right periorbital swelling of three weeks’ duration
No preceding trauma
Treated with ophthalmic ointment and eye drops without improvement
Diagnosed with periorbital cellulitis and prescribed oral cefaclor for two weeks
Swelling and redness persisted
C-reactive protein level of 0.59 mg/dL
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 57 mm/h
Orbital CT scan showed destructive lesion centered on the anterior wall of the right maxillary sinus
MRI showed lesion isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images and heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted images
Mass demonstrated heterogeneous enhancement after contrast administration
Invaded the ipsilateral inferior orbital wall and extraconal space
Adjacent soft-tissue edema and fat infiltration involved the right cheek and periorbital area

per_call: Pleomorphic adenoma of the minor salivary gland

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor with rapid growth, consistent with imaging findings

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Destructive lesion in the maxillary sinus and soft-tissue involvement

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly growing tumor with heterogeneous enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Destructive lesion in the maxillary sinus and involvement of the nasal cavity

shortlist.label: Invasive aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Destructive lesion in the maxillary sinus and rapid progression, despite antibiotic treatment

raw.rationale: The clinical presentation and imaging findings are consistent with a malignant tumor, and Rhabdomyosarcoma is a common orbital malignancy in children, particularly in the age group of the patient.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: While Langerhans cell histiocytosis can cause orbital lesions, the imaging characteristics and aggressive nature of the lesion in this case are more suggestive of Rhabdomyosarcoma.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: Ewing's sarcoma is a possible consideration, but it is less common in the orbit and the imaging findings do not specifically suggest this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
rejected.why: Esthesioneuroblastoma is a rare tumor that typically arises in the nasal cavity and sinuses, and the clinical presentation and imaging findings in this case do not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Invasive aspergillosis
rejected.why: Invasive aspergillosis is an infectious process that can cause orbital inflammation, but the clinical presentation and imaging findings in this case, including the lack of response to antibiotic treatment, suggest a malignant process rather than an infection.
